topics.topic: Ownership of authenticated HTTP routes between deliverer_router and deliverer_api
questions: Does `deliverer_router` own the scan route and delegate to an API handler, or does `deliverer_api` own the authenticated route?
Does `deliverer_router` own the delivery route and delegate to an API handler, or does `deliverer_api` own the authenticated route?
Does `deliverer_router` own the mark route and delegate to an API handler, or does `deliverer_api` own the authenticated route?
Are the HTTP routes owned and declared by `deliverer_router`, with `deliverer_api` supplying their handlers, or are they routes owned by `deliverer_api`?

quotes:
The calling agent is outside this service and organises the work (R0-15). It reads and publishes in the Portal with
its own session. It reaches the deliverer only through the authenticated routes of `module:deliverer_api`, which
delegates to `module:photo_delivery`. The deliverer never calls the Portal. Showing a photo to the client is a later
action of the owner in the Portal and is not part of this flow.
- the routes of the service and the context and token the routes read from the application.
judgement.divergence: One implementation declares the authenticated scan, delivery and mark routes in `deliverer_api`; the other declares them in `deliverer_router` and binds handlers from `deliverer_api`, which the generator and integrator observe in different module surfaces and call graphs.
judgement.why: The owner-delivery flow attributes the authenticated routes to `deliverer_api`, while the module text assigns ownership of the service routes to `deliverer_router`.

topics.topic: Photo delivery request API capability and token-check responsibility
questions: Which `deliverer_api` capability receives the delivery request, and which capability performs the token check?
Which `module:deliverer_api` capability receives the delivery request, performs these checks, and calls `capability:photo_delivery.deliver_project_photo`?

quotes:
`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend/v1` generates, and it holds only what that
backend emits. It imports the route handlers of `deliverer_api`, so `deliverer_api` cannot import it
back. The router declares its extractor of the `Authorization` field and names `check_token` as the
resolver of its one principal, but no route it serves calls them: the health route needs no token, and
every route that does is a handler of `deliverer_api`, which reads the field and calls `check_token`
itself, before the project id or the body.
judgement.why: `deliver_route` receives the delivery request and calls `check_token` before examining the project id or body.

topics.topic: Whether M08 Refusal is owned and exported by domain_models
questions: Is M08 `Refusal` one of the models owned and exported by `domain_models`, despite the ownership list ending at M07, or is it intentionally outside that model list?

quotes:
- the three refusal types: a refusal of the whole operation, a refusal of one file, and
  `AuthenticationRequired`, a request that does not carry the token.

The answer to an operation the service refuses as a whole. `code` says why, and `detail` is a fixed sentence for
people that holds no server path, no credential and nothing the caller sent. Every refused mark is M08. A delivery is M08 for the refusals of
A3 rule 4 and A6 rules 1 and 5, and M06 for the failures of A3 rule 5. A request refused for its token (A5 rule 1) or for
the form of its project id or body is M08 for every operation that requires the token.
judgement.why: M08 is the whole-operation `Refusal` type owned and exported by `domain_models`; it is listed separately from the M01-to-M07 group because the refusal types have their own ownership bullet.
